intent: Count a commit as checked only if its check is less than a day old.

edit.summary:
I changed SKILL.md so that a passing change check counts only while it is less than one day old. I didn't edit EXAMPLES.md or run anything.

- **New property:** `Commit` has an optional `checked_at` property, the time the check was recorded. `record_check` now sets it along with `checks_passed` and `failing`.
- **Approval precondition:** the `checks-pass` precondition on `approve_commit` now needs a passing check younger than a day, unless the commit is `wording_only`. Its reason text tells the owner to re-run the check once it is a day old.
- **Recording precondition:** the `approved-only-if-checked` precondition on `record_approval` has the same freshness condition.
- **Glossary:** the "change check" entry notes the one-day limit.

I left the invariant `approved-commits-passed-their-checks` as it was. If it also used the freshness test, every commit approved more than a day ago would break it.

The spec doesn't say how "now" or the recorded time are defined, so I wrote `now - target.checked_at < 1 day` and "the time of recording" as plain wording. Someone may want to confirm that matches how the kernel supplies time.

findings.problem: The invariant 'approved-commits-passed-their-checks' still only requires checks_passed == true (or wording_only). The change makes approval depend on the check being under a day old, but this invariant was not updated. It is now inconsistent with the approve_commit and record_approval rules. It is also unclear how it would behave as the check ages: an already-approved commit stays valid in the invariant, but a strict freshness check would flip it to failing a day after approval.

Examples that rely on checks_passed true without any checked_at now conflict with the new rule. 'an-approved-commit-gets-a-release-name' and 'a-deputy-approves-while-the-owner-is-away' start with C2 having checks_passed true but no checked_at, so the freshness test cannot be satisfied and step 2 of the deputy example (approve allowed) would be denied. Also, the first example approves right after record_check with no mention of the time; it works only if the check is fresh, and no example covers a stale check being refused.

When checked_at is unset (e.g. commits whose check was recorded before this change, or fixtures), 'now - target.checked_at < 1 day' is undefined. Existing commits with checks_passed true now cannot be approved until re-checked, and the behaviour is not specified. The check also sits in the first half of the checks-pass expression, so checks_passed true with unset checked_at is ambiguous.
